newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Detailed results of D&B Australian business survey.
newsitem.headline: Detailed results of D&B Australian business survey.

text.p: Following are detailed results of Dun and Bradstreet's second quarter Australian business survey released on Thursday.
The survey of about 900 business owners and senior executives among major industry sectors was conducted in March.
(See separate item on the survey overview).
SALES EXPECTATIONS

Sales growth expectations rose four points to an index of 43; sales expectations for non-durables manufacturers rose 17 points. They are much more optimistic than executives in durables manufacturing where the index rose five points. For
retailers the index rose 12 points; the best outlook for growth in retail sales since the end of 1994. Wholesalers were less optimistic; their expected sales index fell four points to 41.
NEW ORDERS EXPECTATIONS

New orders expectations advanced two points and are now 30 points above the low point for the first quarter of 1996. Non-durables manufacturers new orders expectations are very strong having risen 13 points to 60, the best figure since the beginning of 1995. Orders expectations for wholesalers have advanced two points to an index of 44. Durables manufacturers' new orders expectations are weaker than the other sectors and
have fallen three points.
PROFITS EXPECTATIONS

Expectations for higher profits remain unchanged at an index of 3.2, the best figure since the second quarter of 1995. Non-durables manufacturers are, as usual, the most optimistic about profits but have decreased their optimism by seven points to an index of 39. Retailers' profits expectations have recovered by 10 points and are now just about the durables manufactures' index of 30.
SELLING PRICES OUTLOOK

The net proportion of firms expecting to raise selling prices fell from 18 percent to 14 percent. The main factor was a fall in the price expectations of non-durables manufacturers. Their index, which rose last quarter by 11 points to 26, fell back to 12, three points below the index for the fourth quarter of 1996. For wholesalers the selling price expectations index is unchanged at 14; the same as it was three quarters ago and equal to the second lowest level recorded by wholesalers in nine years. Selling price expectations for retailers fell one point.
EMPLOYMENT EXPECTATIONS

Employment expectations was unchanged at an index of 12, the best figure since the third quarter of 1995. Retailers are still the most positive about growth in the number of their expectations of two points. Employment expectations of durables manufacturers rose three points and non-durables manufacturers by two points.
INVENTORY EXPECTATIONS

Inventories expectations rose by three points to an index of nine, with 29 percent expecting an increase, 20 percent a decrease, and 51 percent no change. All sectors are now expecting a rise in inventories, the first time since the end of
1995. Non-durables manufacturers and retailers have the strongest expectations about inventories with net index of 14.
CAPITAL INVESTMENT OUTLOOK

Expectations for increases in capital investment were unchanged at an index of 20 with 28 percent of firms expecting an increase and eight percent a decrease. Non-durables manufacturers are again the most optimistic about increasing capital investment although their index fell three points to 28.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
